We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. Our findings held consistent across various metrics of misinformation, including posts, comments, and shares. Our research also detected regional biases in the dissemination of news from credible sources versus those known for spreading misinformation. Our study highlighted the crucial role of geography in understanding the spread of online misinformation and suggested that addressing this issue could yield significant public policy gains by targeting the influence of population size and local cultural traits. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-supplied domain and over-reliance on domain-agnostic preferences, which is impractical given the ubiquitous sparsity in real-world scenarios. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that tackles multi-target cross-domain recommendation in multiple sparse domains. In contrast to conventional CDR methods, MSDCR considers all participating domains as equally data-poor, thereby simultaneously enhancing the recommendation performance across each domain. We devise a Multi-Domain Separation Network (MDSN) and a Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement (GAPE) module to augment a user's specific aspect preferences in each domain by transferring complementary preferences from other domains, while maintaining domain-specific uniqueness through adversarial training and dynamically determining the degree of complementarity using GAPE. Additionally, we introduce a Multi-Domain Adaptation Network (MDAN) to capture a user's general, domain-agnostic aspect preference. By integrating the domain-specific aspect preference and the domain-agnostic aspect preference, MSDCR attains a thorough understanding of user preferences across each data-poor domain. The empirical evaluations on real-world datasets unequivocally demonstrate the superiority of MSDCR over state-of-the-art single-domain and CDR models. The code has been made available at https://github.com/zwang84/MSDCR

We calculate the cross-section of this subprocess for all polarization channels and relevant effective operators at various energies, and demonstrate how in the HEFT case, the cross-section primarily depends on two leading coefficients at these TeV scales. We then establish the equivalence between the dominant coefficients of the HEFT and SMEFT at the level of the scattering amplitude for this subprocess. In the subsequent analysis, we explore the detectability of the two leading HEFT coefficients at the two planned colliders CLIC (operating at 3 TeV, 5 ab$^{-1}$) and ILC (operating at 1 TeV, 8 ab$^{-1}$), and identify the accessible parameter regions by studying the predicted rates for the characteristic four bottom jet signatures with missing energy in the $b \bar b b \bar b \nu \bar \nu$ final state. We also consider and reject the possibility of equivalent signals arising from the $WW \to HH$ subprocess in the SM at these colliders

During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals struggle to contribute effectively. Our proposed framework, Spatially-Aware Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (SABRA), mitigates the impact of false positives in VRD tasks. Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric and semi-metric spaces. Building upon this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. Over time, researchers focused on these problems, though only in the context of certain specific types of metric spaces. This article aims to enhance the definition of angle function to accommodate spaces with the property of betweenness, which it deems a more fundamental framework. Within this revised framework, the article provides solutions to Menger's initially posed problems. As a result, it offers a new, streamlined proof of the theorem that spaces with angle functions are equivalent to spaces with the property of betweenness. As an added consequence, the article also establishes the direct connection between the problem of embedding a space with the property of betweenness into a Euclidean space and the problem of defining a Euclidean structure on this space. Furthermore, the article introduces a new, specific type of space with the property of betweenness, which it calls the S-space, and provides a embedding of the S-space into a Euclidean space. As a corollary, the article is able to provide a solution to the second of Menger's initially posed problems regarding the embedding of certain metric spaces. The article concludes with an exploration of the relationship between the concept of angle function and the property of betweenness in the context of the so-called uniform spaces. As an additional

One significant limitation of existing text-based games lies in their slow speed, topping out at around 300 actions per second, largely because of outdated technology used to create them.
Our research presents TextWorldExpress, a highly optimized version of three widely used text-based game challenges, achieving a remarkable increase in simulation processing speed of roughly three orders of magnitude.
On ordinary computer hardware, it can process over one million actions per second, allowing for extensive tests lasting merely a day rather than weeks or even months. 
Our results show that modern, high-speed versions of these games reveal distinct challenges and strategies, revealing that agents now suffer from a new problem called "information overload".
They also discover that agents can succeed with much simpler conversation-based problem-solving strategies than before.
Additionally, TextWorldExpress facilitates easy plugin integration for various cutting-edge techniques like neural networks, making it an ideal platform for testing the latest virtual agent technologies. 
We have made TextWorldExpress publicly available on a dedicated website, inviting participants to take part in a global challenge to enhance it further.  We also present the express edition of a renowned text-based game league, providing a benchmark score for anyone to beat.  All game data, including the league, is accessible via the website. A plasma source with a 0.1 meter length and 0.4 meter diameter provides plasma necessary for the experiment, and features a helical antenna to produce high-density plasma in the helicon mode of discharge. Until now, it was unclear if this plasma source could achieve helicon mode, which is essential for it to function effectively. A study was conducted to verify this capability, involving detailed analysis of plasma parameters and particle power balance using a global model. The plasma source that was tested is now being used for a variety of applications including testing components for the ITER device, researching the effects of errors on plasma behavior, and studying the effects of plasma on radio frequency waves. In this research, a concept for GAN-based medical imaging enhancement is demonstrated. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. Our research was showcased at the Medical Imaging meets NeurIPS Workshop 2020, a satellite event of the 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems held in Vancouver, Canada. This research paves the way for utilizing GAN-based techniques in medical imaging, opening up exciting possibilities for using such models in real-world healthcare scenarios. In addition to presenting our findings, we also highlighted potential challenges, unexplored aspects, and future directions for utilizing GAN-based medical imaging. Although significant progress has been made, there is still much unexplored potential in medical imaging, and our research encourages further innovation in this field.
